hero.tagline: I build full-stack platforms, games and systems software — and I host them myself.
hero.sub: Computer Engineering student from Penedono (Viseu), studying in Oliveira do Hospital, Portugal. Everything below runs for real: each platform in its own Docker container, served from my homelab.

about.title: About me
about.p1: I'm André, a Computer Engineering student — curious by nature, with a particular pull towards cybersecurity, and always looking for the next thing to learn. My projects aren't tutorial clones — they're platforms with real databases, real auth, and real bugs I had to track down and fix, deployed on infrastructure I run myself.
about.p2: What I enjoy most is the full path: designing the data layer, building the API on top, giving it a clean UI, then containerizing the whole thing and putting it behind a reverse proxy on my own hardware.
about.aiText: I've been using Claude Code in my daily workflow since February 2026 — for code review and security passes. The point isn't delegating everything: it's orchestrating AI tools inside a workflow I control. I also run my own self-hosted AI agent, connected to a few personal services, with persistent memory — on my homelab, not someone else's cloud.

stack.title: Stack
stack.sub: Languages, frameworks and tools I actually use in the projects below.

platforms.title: Live Platforms
platforms.sub: Full platforms you can actually use — each one dockerized and self-hosted on my homelab, exposed through a secure tunnel.

voltexchange.desc: Peer-to-peer energy trading platform. Users register smart meters, submit readings, and buy/sell surplus energy on an open market — matched automatically inside the database.
highlights: PostgreSQL does the heavy lifting: 24 monthly range partitions over 500k readings, a stored-procedure matching engine, anomaly-detection triggers
The UI deliberately exposes the database internals — partition pruning, trigger firings and quarantine procedures are part of the demo
Rate limiting, helmet, parameterized queries throughout

travel.desc: Trip planning platform: search flights and hotels, save trips, manage your account. OAuth login (Google/GitHub), transactional email via Resend, and an AI trip planner shown as a token-free demo.
highlights: Real OAuth authorization-code flow with account-hijack protection (verified-email checks)
Airport/city search backed by an open-data dataset after the Amadeus self-service API closed
AI planner presented honestly: a scripted preview instead of burning API tokens per visitor

folio.desc: Investment portfolio tracker. Track stocks, ETFs and crypto with live prices, daily snapshots, bulk import from CSV/Excel, and email-verified accounts.
highlights: Spring Boot backend with a batch price pipeline and a materialized view for the public market highlights
4-character email verification and password-reset codes via Resend
Bulk import that reports per-row errors without aborting the whole file

millionaire.desc: "Who Wants to Be a Millionaire" — a playable quiz game with a Laravel API behind it: JWT auth, question management and score tracking.
highlights: Originally two separate repos (API + frontend), merged and dockerized as one platform
Dynamic gameplay built in vanilla JS — no framework, straight DOM manipulation and API calls

gamelobby.desc: "TV Time for games" — track what you're playing, rate it, review it. Game data comes live from the IGDB API.
highlights: Live game data pulled from the IGDB API — search, cover art and metadata synced straight from Twitch's game database
Legacy PHP codebase, session-based auth with bcrypt password hashing

kits.desc: Packing list manager — build reusable kits for trips and activities so you never forget the charger again.
highlights: Laravel API + Svelte frontend behind an nginx proxy, Sanctum session auth

ecofuturo.desc: Educational platform that teaches children about the environment through games and puzzles.
highlights: One of my earliest server-side projects — kept online as part of the progression story

projects.title: Projects
projects.sub: Games, systems programming and mobile work.

netherfall.desc: Top-down survival game built with Pygame — v2 of my Vampire Survivors-inspired project, rebuilt with better architecture, save system and progression. Compiled to WebAssembly (pygbag) — playable right here in your browser.

f1page.desc: HTML & CSS-only fan page for the Netflix series Drive to Survive — my first "real" project, kept here to show the progression.

repairflow.desc: Repair-shop management in two takes: a terminal app with a clean service/DAO architecture, then the same architecture evolved into a Java Swing GUI.

healthcenter.desc: Health center management system — final project for my programming course, service/DAO architecture in Java.

repairshop.desc: Repair shop in C: type tables, linked lists per service/component, recursion, and binary-file persistence. Data Structures coursework turned standalone project.

gamestore.desc: Terminal-based game store management system in Java.

storec.desc: Terminal-based store management system in C.

androidapps.desc: Collection of native Android apps built with Kotlin and Android Studio.

qrscanner.desc: QR Safe Scanner — a real product in launch phase: scans QR codes and runs the target through a 5-layer safety verification pipeline before you open it. Closed source (Stripe billing, Trial/Pro/Premium plans).

homelab.title: Homelab & Infrastructure
homelab.sub: The part that doesn't show up in a repo: everything on this site runs on hardware I manage.

proxmox.title: Virtualization & isolation
proxmox.desc: A hypervisor running isolated containers, one per service — the platforms above plus a handful of other self-hosted tools, never sharing a box.

edge.title: Tunnel + reverse proxy
edge.desc: No open ports on my router: a tunnel brings traffic in from the internet, and a reverse proxy routes each subdomain to the right container with TLS handled centrally.

hera.title: Personal automation agent
hera.desc: A self-built, self-hosted assistant connected to a few of my personal services, with persistent memory — running on my own hardware, not a third-party cloud.

email.title: Transactional email
email.desc: A verified sending domain — account verification and password-reset emails for the platforms that need them.
